verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report correlations between circulating irisin and an anthropometric measure. Study A (PMID 30641808) reports a significant positive correlation between serum irisin and BMI (r = 0.374, P = 0.004) in type II diabetic patients, and Study B (PMID 40643080) reports a significant negative correlation between plasma irisin and waist circumference (r = -0.272, p = 0.024) in a Brazilian cohort. BMI and waist circumference are both anthropometric adiposity measures, so the two findings address a similar exposure-outcome relationship but with opposite directions. Neither abstract provides a text-supported contextual difference (e.g., population, assay, or adjustment) that would explain the discrepancy, so the pair is classified as contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: Serum irisin levels showed a significant positive correlation with BMI (r = 0.374, P = 0.004)
Irisin was negatively correlated with weight (r = -0.246; p = 0.042), waist circumference (r = -0.272; p = 0.024)

diagnostics.notes: Both claims are unadjusted correlation analyses of circulating irisin vs. an anthropometric measure; directions are opposite (+ vs -). No explicit explanatory difference is stated in either abstract.
